generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The check for link-local addresses `(ipv6[0] == (byte) 0xfe && ipv6[1] == (byte) 0x80)` only identifies addresses starting with the `fe80::/64` prefix. According to RFC 4291, IPv6 link-local addresses are defined by the prefix `fe80::/10`, meaning the second byte can be any value from `0x80` to `0xBF`. To fully comply with the specification, consider using a bitmask: `(ipv6[0] == (byte) 0xfe && (ipv6[1] & 0xc0) == (byte) 0x80)`.

review_comment: Reading through the man page, it sounds like scope is _only_ supported for link-local addresses. Does that means we should omit the scope, even non-zero scope, if the address is not link local?
I asked myself the same but then decided against it as we should only fill it with non-zero when the underlying OS tells us so..
